body:
Observed 2026-08-14 while measuring the blast radius of #1331 (PR #1602).

`tests/unit/test_1596_module_entry_point.py` fails four tests on a clean
`origin/main` checkout (815632762) under `repo/.venv`:

- TestModuleEntryPoint::test_module_is_executable_from_an_unrelated_cwd
- TestModuleEntryPoint::test_help_names_the_program_not_the_dunder_file
- TestCwdCannotShadowTheApplication::test_minus_P_ignores_a_cps_sitting_in_the_cwd[module]
- TestCwdCannotShadowTheApplication::test_minus_P_ignores_a_cps_sitting_in_the_cwd[package]

CI is green on the same commit, so this is an environment difference, not a
repo regression — these tests spawn `python -m cps` from an unrelated working
directory, which needs the package importable from somewhere other than the
checkout. The venv the tick uses does not have it installed.

Why it matters rather than being a local annoyance: a red local suite is what
wedges a tick. A pass that runs the unit suite before merging has to A/B every
failure against main to find out whether it caused it, and the next pass pays
the same cost again. The failure also teaches sessions to read a red suite as
normal, which is exactly how a real regression gets waved through.

Fix is either an editable install in the documented local-dev venv setup, or a
skip guarded on `cps` being importable from outside the checkout with a reason
that names this. Not fixed here — it is outside #1331's diff and #1596 is
recent enough that its author's intent should be read first.

MEASURED, not inferred: the same four fail on the unmodified main worktree in
the same environment; 6009 tests pass around them.
title: Four unit tests fail on a clean local checkout but pass in CI
